svg.title: How to read the power-number chart (MSH Fig. 9.12)
svg.text: How to read the power-number chart (MSH Fig. 9.12)
Reynolds number, Re = Dₐ² n ρ / μ
Power number, Np = P g꜀ / (ρ n³ Dₐ⁵)
A, B, C: flat-blade six-blade turbines, 4 baffles; D: unbaffled (dashed: × Fr^m)
Compute Re = D_a² n ρ/μ and mark it on the bottom axis.
Pick the curve for your impeller and tank from the shape-factor table (here A: S₄ = 0.2, 4 baffles); go up to it.
Go across to the left axis.
Read Np, then P = Np ρ n³ Dₐ⁵ (SI) or ÷ g_c (fps). Unbaffled curve D above Re ≈ 300: × Fr^m.
Redrawn from MSH 5th ed. Fig. 9.12 (digitized; turbulent level of curve A taken as 5.8,
as read in MSH Example 9.3); in the exam read the printed chart — values may differ slightly.
